description: Landing copy whose promises are unverifiable, unexplained, or contradicted by the company's own history. Best run as a `react` panel — the flaws surface as behaviour, not as verdicts.

flaws.description: The page promises a ceiling but never says what happens when you hit it — throttled, charged, emailed, cut off? This is the first question any buyer asks and the page stops there.
A pricing page with no price on it. The headline promises control over a number it never shows.
'No surprises. Ever.' is an absolute promise about billing, made by a company whose own support queue is full of surprise-bill complaints. It reads as the claim it is trying to disprove.
'Save an average of 40%' has no methodology, no sample and no basis anyone can check — and it cannot be true for every account, since usage pricing raises some bills.
Customer logos in the footer with no indication of permission — and at least one of these accounts is a churn risk or has already left.
'Thousands of companies' and 'teams who hate surprises' are unfalsifiable filler that any competitor could copy verbatim.
'Set a ceiling' is a cost-control promise; 'grow into it' is a growth pitch. The page runs both at once and commits to neither.
